author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Fitbit: An ‘Underappreciated’ Opportunity That Needs ‘Time’
text:
Photo: Getty Images By David Marino-Nachison June 20, 2018 11:42 a.m. ET Shares of Fitbit (FIT), up roughly 20% this year, got another boost Wednesday morning as William Blair started coverage of the company with a cautiously optimistic take saying “the company’s health care related opportunity is underappreciated.”
Recent history for the company has been well-told; first hot as a fitness tracker company, it’s now trying to transform itself into a company that can be seen as both a valuable smartwatch maker and a leader in digital health tracking.
Newsletter Sign-up As investors have bought into the story , the company’s shares have responded. William Blair, for its part, said it expects “the transition, particularly on the face of the income statement, to take some time.”
Consequently, it called “the current risk/reward in Fitbit as balanced.” Wall Street, broadly, seems to feel about the same, with most of the analysts tracked by FactSet reporting “hold” ratings and the mean share price target around $6, below current levels.
William Blair sees Fitbit as a well-branded company positioned to benefit from “a significant additional market opportunity for an ecosystem that improves employee health outcomes and reduces employer health care expenditures, on top of the market for consumer wearables.
Illustration: William Blair But they don’t see victory as clear-cut—hence the aforementioned caution. There’s competition, for one, notably in the smartwatch category, where fellow Barron’s Next 50 company Apple (AAPL) has quickly become a power ; its products compete for space on the body and in the budget.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 And the comparatively new industry has yet to show it can deliver recurring subscription revenue from mainstream consumers.
“Fitbit’s active and engaged user base and investment in developing greater software based innovation present an interesting opportunity to monetize, but it may take a few different tries at the business model (e.g., freemium, paid-only subscriptions, per use models) to generate meaningful and lasting growth,” wrote William Blair.
